## The Object

```text
c_(p,q)(beta) = sum_{mode in Z} D_mode,
D_mode = det[ I_{mode + lam_j + i - j}(t) ]_{i,j = 0,1,2},   t = beta/3,
lam = (p+q, q, 0),   sum lam = p + 2q
```

(the SU(3) Weyl character formula; the runner reads `lam` from
`highest_weight_triple` and `D_mode` from the exact 3x3 `iv`-determinant). W89
MEASURED that a FIXED mode window leaves 25-34% of the mass outside — a fixed
cutoff does not dominate the tail. The runner reproduces this (the fixed
`|mode| > 5` tail grows `1.6e-2 -> 3.4e-1` as `beta` grows), confirming a
`beta`-scaled window is required.

## The Derivation (via W87)

Factor `e^{3t}` (the determinant is a sum of products of three entries):

```text
e^{-3t} D_mode = det[ e^{-t} I_{nu_ij}(t) ],   nu_ij = mode + lam_j + i - j.
```

For active weights `a = weight/sqrt(beta) = O(1)`, the indices are `nu_ij =
O(sqrt(t))` while `t = beta/3 = O(beta)`, so `nu_ij = O(sqrt(t))` — exactly the
W87 regime. By the W87 uniform Bessel local-CLT, each entry is a Gaussian of
width `sqrt(t)` in its index:

```text
e^{-t} I_{nu_ij}(t) ~ (2 pi t)^(-1/2) exp( -nu_ij^2 / (2t) ) (1 + O(1/sqrt t)).
```

The 3x3 determinant of these Gaussians, as a function of `mode`, is itself a
Gaussian in `(mode - mode_peak)` of width `O(sqrt(t))`, centered at the value
that balances the indices,

```text
mode_peak = -round( (sum lam)/3 ) = -round( (p + 2q)/3 ).
```

(The center minimizes `sum_ij nu_ij^2`-type weight; the runner confirms
`mode_peak` exactly on every tested case.) The tail beyond an `A sqrt(t)` window
is then the Gaussian tail:

```text
sum_{|mode - mode_peak| > A sqrt(t)} |D_mode|  <=  g(A) * sum_mode |D_mode|,
g(A) ~ exp(-c A^2),   c ~ 1.60,
```

uniform in `beta` and across the bounded active-weight window. This is the
determinant-level shadow of the same `sqrt(t)` local-CLT scaling W87 proved at
the scalar level: the mode window must scale as `sqrt(t) = sqrt(beta/3)`, not as
a fixed cutoff.

## Witnessed Uniform Constants (not fitted)

The runner computes `g(A)` from the EXACT 3x3 Bessel determinants across
`beta in {48,108,192,300}` and active weights `p,q ~ sqrt(beta)`:

| A (window = A sqrt t) | g(A) range over all cases |
|---:|---|
| 2 | 2.1e-4 .. 3.8e-4 (flat ~3e-4) |
| 3 | 7.2e-8 .. 1.3e-7 (flat ~1e-7) |

`g(2)` varies by `< 2x` (measured spread `1.80x`; runner gate `< 3x`) and `g(3)`
likewise across the whole sampled `beta`/active-weight grid (uniformity), and the
implied Gaussian rate `c = ln(g2/g3)/(9-4)` is stable at `1.59-1.60`. The constants
are witnessed (computed from the exact determinants), not fitted; the derivation
via W87 supplies the `exp(-c A^2)` form and the `sqrt(t)` scaling. The witnessed
`c ~ 1.60` is the effective rate over the `A in {2,3}` grid (a discrete sum of a
Gaussian profile has a mildly `A`-dependent effective rate); it is not claimed as
a single rigorous asymptotic determinant-local-CLT constant. The load-bearing
output is the active-window uniform tail form `exp(-c A^2)` with some `c > 0`.

## Anti-Fabrication

`g(A)` is computed from `np.linalg.det` of exact `I_nu(t)` entries; no
`curve_fit`/`polyfit`, no target value, no closure constant. `mode_peak =
-round((p+2q)/3)` is derived (the index-balancing center) and confirmed exactly.
The `exp(-c A^2)` form and `sqrt(t)` scaling come from W87 (derived), not from a
fit.

## Falsifiers

- A FIXED window (not `sqrt(t)`-scaled) does NOT give a uniform tail: the
  `|mode-peak| > 5` tail grows `1.6e-2 -> 3.4e-1` with `beta` (the W88/W89 25-34%
  problem) — confirming the `sqrt(t)` scaling is necessary.
- A WRONG center (e.g. `mode = 0` instead of `-round((p+2q)/3)`) inflates the
  `2 sqrt(t)` tail from `3.8e-4` to `0.27` — confirming the peak location.

## Honest Outcome

H_det piece (2) — the determinant-mode tail domination on the active
`p,q <= A sqrt(beta)` weight window: the mode sum is dominated by the
`|mode - mode_peak| <= A sqrt(t)` window (`mode_peak = -round((p+2q)/3)`), with
tail form `<= g(A) ~ exp(-c A^2)` for some `c > 0` — is derived (via W87's Bessel
local-CLT) and witnessed. The runner's `c ~ 1.60` is a finite-grid effective rate,
not a separately asserted rigorous constant. H_det piece (3) the outside-weight
tail remains open; H_det and the half-line gap theorem are NOT closed by this
note. The next path this opens: piece (3) (the Gaussian `exp(-Q(a))` weight-sum
tail), after which H_det's `K_W(A)` assembles with W87 (H_scalar) and W91 (the
`c_(0,0)` lower bound).
